report:
Fresh complete followup assessment of test_coverage against current inputs. Latest shared spec.rs delta adds only an implementation_references association above the unknown-implementation validator; it does not change the coverage algorithm. The entire present claim and both associated tests were nevertheless reassessed.

The claim requires at least one annotated Rust test per specification anchor, missing tests to fail independently of implementation coverage, placeholder tests to count while retaining their explicit status, and implementation placeholders alone not to satisfy test coverage. The sole associated ordinary implementation validate_anchors iterates every anchor and emits the missing-test diagnostic when the tests map has no key or an empty vector. It reads no implementation inventory and makes no status-based exemption, so an ordinary or placeholder implementation cannot supply a test entry. The captured spec.rs also shows validate invokes this check separately from implementation validation. The inspected correspondence dependency accepts module-level annotated test declarations into the test map; the review inventory dependency copies those tests and determines status from the owning module through the captured placeholder_status helper. That helper explicitly preserves TODO/N/A ancestry rather than interpreting the entry as ordinary execution proof. These supporting helpers implement general annotation/status infrastructure; the associated validate_anchors owns the claim's coverage requirement.

Both ordinary test bodies provide meaningful assertions. test_coverage_is_bidirectional_and_allows_many_to_many_links first supplies multiple entries for the first anchor and one for the second and requires validation success. It then empties the second anchor vector and adds an unknown test reference; it requires exactly two diagnostics, identifies the missing-test error with the definition source and anchor name, and separately checks the unknown-reference source/span/message. This exercises the empty-entry failure and at-least-one success without an implementation precondition. implementation_placeholders_do_not_replace_explicit_placeholder_tests uses actual Rust source indexing, with TODO and N/A implementation comments for two anchors. It requires successful implementation validation, no test entries, and exactly two missing-test errors. It then appends explicitly annotated TODO and N/A test functions, requires clean indexing and test validation, and asserts exactly one review test per anchor with Todo and NotApplicable status respectively. This directly establishes missing-key failure, independence of implementation coverage, and acceptance without status erasure for both placeholder kinds.

The source/test_site helper capture was inspected: the former preserves input text; the latter constructs a stable RustSite for the map-level unit test, so that test is not represented as a full annotation-parser test. The actual-source placeholder test supplies the complementary integration path. Additional captured dependencies are correspondence::record_tests, review test inventory construction, and evidence::placeholder_status. There are no TODO/N/A evidence entries for this anchor itself and no deferred clause.

This was source review with fresh start/read/record commands, not a blind refresh. No source changes or test reruns were performed in this review; the coordinator reports central suites passed. All claim aspects are covered by current implementation and substantive assertions. No requested edits.
